page: Microsoft Azure D64ns_v6 belongs to the general-purpose Dnv6 family, hosted on Microsoft Hyper-V. The virtual machine provides 64 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 32 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8573C processor using the x86_64 architecture with a maximum clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The CPU subsystem includes 260 MB of L3 cache along with support for advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel AMX. System memory totals 256.0 GB of RAM, maintaining a balanced ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. The instance does not bundle local disk storage or hardware accelerators such as GPUs, requiring remote network-attached block storage for persistent data.

Benchmark evaluations reveal strong parallel execution, cryptographic processing, and instruction set acceleration. In PassMark tests, the instance records top-quartile results across overall CPU score (67,051.45), extended instructions (71,083.39), and encryption throughput (56,353.15). Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression achieves 347.46 GB/sec, placing in the top 25 percent. In-memory data handling demonstrates 71.06 million Redis SET operations per second and 90.06 GB/sec of static web serving throughput. CPU-based machine learning inference shows strong prompt processing rates across small, medium, and large models. In contrast, PassMark memory performance scored in the bottom 25 percent, while uncached large-block memory read and write bandwidth remain in the middle tier.

Given the 64-core density and balanced memory allocation without local disks, the D64ns_v6 delivers resource density for compute-intensive networked environments. Architectural tradeoffs include the complete absence of bundled local storage, requiring network I/O planning for disk-heavy operations. The instance is suited for high-throughput static web serving, distributed caching with Redis, relational and non-relational database services utilizing remote Premium Storage, container orchestration, and multi-threaded ETL pipelines.
